The Actually-Free Job Training Directory

Zero-dollar upskilling: university courses in audit mode, library learning platforms, free certificates, state workforce programs, and CEU samplers for health workers.

5 categories, 28 offers. Last verified: 2026-11-08. No ads, no affiliates, no tracking.

How to read every entry

  • Every offer listed here costs $0.00 to use in the way described. If an offer later grows a paywall, it gets flagged and fixed or removed.
  • Nobody in this directory pays us. There are no affiliate links, no referral codes, and no tracking parameters on any URL.
  • Each entry says exactly what "free" means for that offer: free everywhere, free with a library card, free course content but paid paper, or a government check that pays tuition for you.
  • Certificates and CEUs matter or they don't exist here: if an entry mentions a paper trail, the entry tells you whether that paper is free.

University Courses in Audit Mode

Real university course material you can read, watch, and work through without paying. In almost every case the catch is the same: no graded feedback and no certificate. You trade the paper for the knowledge.
MIT OpenCourseWare — Massachusetts Institute of Technology · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://ocw.mit.edu

What it is: About 2,500 complete MIT courses published openly: lecture videos, notes, assignments, and often exams with solutions. Good for business, math, computer science, and engineering basics.

What “free” means: 100% free. No account, no limits, no trial timer. Everything meaningful on the site is free.

Paper trail: None. There is no certificate at any price, and no instructor responds to questions.

Time needed: A few hours to skim a course; 30-80 study hours for a full one

Honest catch: No credit, no credential, no human support. You organize your own learning.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: university, no-signup, self-paced, career, tech, stem

MIT Open Learning Library — Massachusetts Institute of Technology · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://openlearninglibrary.mit.edu

What it is: A hosted platform version of selected MIT courses with auto-graded exercises, chat-forum-style help threads, and interactive problem sets.

What “free” means: 100% free. A free account is required to save progress. No payment step exists.

Paper trail: None for most courses. Some issue scans of your work as progress proof, not certificates.

Time needed: 10-100 study hours depending on the course

Honest catch: Small course list (tens, not thousands). No credit. Certificates generally unavailable even paid.

Learning Platforms Via Your Library Card

Public libraries (and state libraries) in the US often pay for huge learning platforms, then hand them to cardholders at no charge. You may already be paying for these locally, so this is the closest thing to money-for-nothing in the directory.
Gale Courses — Gale (Cengage) via public libraries · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.gale.com/c/galecourses

What it is: Six-week, instructor-led courses on job and life skills: business writing, grant writing, computers, healthcare-related workplace skills, personal finance.

What “free” means: Free through participating public libraries: your card number (plus a free learner account) is tuition. New sessions start monthly.

Paper trail: Free certificate of completion for finishing quizzes/assignments.

Time needed: 2-4 hours per week for 6 weeks, with instructors available

Honest catch: Only works if your local library subscribes (check the library chooser inside the product). Course material can feel slightly dated.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: library-card, certificate, instructor-led, career

Universal Class — Universal Class via public libraries · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.universalclass.com

What it is: 500+ online courses across office skills, computers, care work, office administration, and 'How-Tos for jobs' with real human-paced lessons.

What “free” means: Free through thousands of participating public libraries; card number is tuition. Courses include CEUs (Continuing Education Units) from an IACET-recognized provider at no cost through the library.

Paper trail: Course certificate and CEU documentation for most courses.

Time needed: Per-course: usually 8-20 hours, up to 6 months to finish

Honest catch: Library-sponsor access usually caps you at a handful of concurrent courses. CEUs are continuing-education units, not college credit.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: library-card, ceu, certificate, self-paced

LearningExpress Library — EBSCO via public/state libraries · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.learningexpresshub.com

What it is: Practice exams and course videos for job-track certification tests: civil service, nursing school entry, CDL (commercial driver), cosmetology, and high-school equivalency (GED/HiSET).

What “free” means: Free through participating libraries; card number is the pass. Includes course videos, e-books, and full practice-test banks.

Paper trail: Scores and progress only. The actual credential comes if you pass the real-world exam this prepares you for.

Time needed: Per-exam track: often 10-40 hours of practice

Honest catch: Institutional access only: you need a library that subscribes. Exam content is study material, not instruction in a skilled trade.

Free Certificates (Google, Cloud Basics & More)

These hand you an actual certificate or digital badge at zero cost — including Google tools and cloud basics from AWS, Cisco, and IBM. These are the 'yes, that line goes on the resume' items. Every free claim here includes the certificate itself.
Google Skillshop — Google · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://skillshop.withgoogle.com

What it is: Google's own training platform: Google Ads certifications, Google Analytics 4 certifications, Google Workspace skills, and AI/ML basics tracks.

What “free” means: 100% free including exams and certificates; any Google account gets in. No trial, no card on file.

Paper trail: Shareable digital certificates (searchable/recruiter-visible in Google Partner contexts).

Time needed: 3-20 hours per certification track

Honest catch: Google Ads certifications expire after about a year and must be re-taken free. Training glorifies Google's own tools.

State & Federal Workforce Programs (US)

Government programs that can pay for real training, coaching, and placement for job seekers. Rule of thumb: the help is free, and in some cases the institution is the payer of training you could never afford. Distance and eligibility are the keys.
CareerOneStop — U.S. Department of Labor · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.careeronestop.org

What it is: The government's umbrella career site: training finder, WIOA-eligible training provider lists, apprenticeship search, short-term certificate search, and state-specific program links.

What “free” means: 100% free, no signup for most features. Federal-payer tools; nothing on the site asks for money.

Paper trail: None. It is a directory/mapper for programs that have their own paperwork.

Time needed: 30 minutes bookmarking; hours if you work the training lists

Honest catch: Destined to feel a bit bureaucratic: data quality varies by state, and eligibility facts live on program-by-program pages.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: government, no-signup, career, wioa

America's Job Centers (locator) — U.S. Department of Labor via CareerOneStop · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.careeronestop.org/LocalHelp/local-help.aspx

What it is: The official finder for American Job Centers: walk-in centers with free career coaching, resume help, workshops, and staff who actually process WIOA training-scholarship applications.

What “free” means: Center services are free to job seekers. WIOA-funded training can make tuition at approved schools $0 for eligible people (displaced workers, income thresholds apply).

Paper trail: Any WIOA funding paperwork happens through the center; outcomes can include funded certificates or community-college seats.

Time needed: 1-hour visit to start; weeks to process full funding cases

Honest catch: Funding is competitive and capped per area, so words like 'you may qualify' carry real waitlist energy. Bring ID, work history, and income paperwork.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: government, funded-teaching, in-person, wioa

WorkOne (Indiana) — Indiana Department of Workforce Development · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.in.gov/dwd/workone/

What it is: Indiana's public workforce centers: free career advising, employer-match services, and a path to state-backed training money (WIOA grants, plus the Workforce Ready Grant which covers adult students' costs at Ivy Tech and other schools).

What “free” means: Center help is free. The Workforce Ready Grant is need-based no-repayment state aid for adult learners in designated high-value certificate programs (so it is state-funded, not out of your pocket).

Paper trail: Everything is application-and-document-tax: WIOA and grant approvals land real funded certificates or programs.

Time needed: First visit under 2 hours; funding windows vary

Honest catch: Indiana-specific. Some qualifying programs list waitlists; actual amounts depend on the program year.

Michigan Reconnect — State of Michigan · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.michigan.gov/reconnect

What it is: A Michigan program covering tuition for adults 25+ who lack a college degree, at community colleges for in-district students, plus a skills-scholarship path for short-term training.

What “free” means: Free tuition at your in-district community college if you meet residency and eligibility basics. This is a state-offset program, so the applicant pays nothing when in-district.

Paper trail: You enroll at the community college but the state pays tuition; credential is the actual college credit/certificate.

Time needed: Semesters: one to two years for associate degrees.

Honest catch: Michigan residents only; out-of-district or private schools cost money that the program may not cover fully. Confirm current eligibility rules before enrolling.

Link: https://launch.idaho.gov

What it is: A state grant for Idaho adults 22+ toward a short-term credential-bearing training program (CDL, welding, tech certifications, trades).

Health CEU Samplers (Licensed Professionals)

Free continuing-education units for nurses, therapists, and other licensed health workers. These are samplers: real CE credit on specific courses, with rotating catalogs. Always confirm with your licensing board that a course counts for your renewal. Education only; nothing here is medical advice.
TRAIN Learning Network — Public Health Foundation · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.train.org

What it is: Thousands of public-health courses from CDC, states, universities, and nonprofits, organized in one searchable catalog with completion transcripts.

What “free” means: Free account, free courses. Many courses carry CE credit (nursing CNE, CHES, and more) at no charge; the accreditation line is on each course page.

Paper trail: Free certificates of completion; legitimate CE certificates where the course's accreditation line says so.

Time needed: 30 minutes to several hours per course

Honest catch: Catalog quality varies by source. Confirm the course lists your specific credit type (e.g., CNE) before counting it toward renewal.

Verified free on 2026-11-08 · re-check due by 2027-01-08 · tags: ceu, health, sign-up, certificate

CDC TRAIN — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.train.org/cdctrain

What it is: CDC's own branch of the TRAIN network: CDC publications, outbreak-response courses, vaccine science, disease-prevention, and self-care-style public-health content.

What “free” means: Free account, free courses. CDC is an accredited continuing-education provider, so most courses that offer credit list CNE (nursing), and others list credit for specific professions.

Paper trail: Free CE certificates for completed activities where the accreditation is stated.

Time needed: 30 minutes to 6 hours per activity

Honest catch: Not every course is CE-bearing. Look at the 'CE offered' list on each activity page before counting hours.

What it is: The Alzheimer's Association's curated e-learning library on dementia care: recognizing change, communication approaches, and care-partner support.

What “free” means: Free course content; some courses in the library include CE certificates at no cost. Look for the CE flag per course; the rest you take for free without credit.

Medscape CE — WebMD/Medscape · verified free 2026-11-08

Link: https://www.medscape.org

What it is: Clinician-targeted CE articles, case activities, and panels across nearly every specialty. Browsers block access when they see them coming, but the site functions well in a normal browser window.

What “free” means: Free for clinicians with a free account: most CE activities across CME for physicians and CE for nurses are sponsored, so you pay nothing.

Paper trail: Free CE certificates; your transcript builds over time inside your Medscape account.

Time needed: 15 minutes to 2 hours per activity

Honest catch: Activity catalogs rotate as sponsorships rotate. Some CNE sponsors do not license your state's credit types. Bots and script checks can 429-block the site.
